Cold, bland and hairy.
Dec 2023 • Couples
We chose to eat here due to good reviews on tripadvisor. If I’d realised where this restaurant actually was I would never have gone and would have understood why some people think this is good food. 

The eatery is a stone’s throw from Bui Viên street, the Disneylandesque (if Snow White was a prostitute) drinking street, which should tell you all you need to know about the quality of the food here. If not, read on…

When the meal arrived it was cold (as many meals tend to be across Vietnam), and came with someone’s hair in it. When I waved the hair at the waitress she just stared, unconcerned that someone else’s mane in my meal could constitute a problem. 

I had the Vietnamese curry. Curry by name but sadly not by nature, it was more like coronation chicken than curry and the spring rolls we had as an accompaniment were literally dripping in vegetable oil.

The food was cheap, but it really wasn’t an enjoyable meal. I can honestly say we had substantially better food (if a similar temperature) all across the country. Largely from small eateries by the side of roads. 

If you want decent food, head away from the tourist traps, grab a small stool on the street and eat local - you’ll enjoy it a lot more!

Found this little gem by accident. Having a wander around Ho Chi Minh and spotted a sign for happy hour priced beer with Saigon beer for 13K (around 0.80 AUD) each so decided to stop in for a coldie and a rest from the unrelenting heat of HCM City.
Location - good as it is hidden away down an alley way where there are not quite so many hawkers. We still had a few, but nowhere near as many as sitting in a cafe on a busier road.
Service - awesome! Our waiter was very young, but very attentive. I did not have to wait for anything, as soon as we finished a beer/drink, he was at the table asking if we needed refills. We decided to have a bite while here, and the food did not disappoint. I had the bacon wrapped vegetable rolls (around $2 AUD) and my partner had satay crocodile skewers (around $3 AUD). The food here is fairly simple, but is very fresh and well cooked; and you can tell that the ingredients used are good quality.
Pricing is fantastic. Maybe a little more than typical street food; but still very reasonable. We paid all up around 240K VND (around $16 AUD) for both our meals and around 8 beers. 
We decided to return again before we left HCM City and service and food quality was excellent on our second visit.
If you want pretentious, overpriced snobby food, this is not the place for you. But if you are looking for a lovely little spot with some cheap beer and nicely cooked simple food, then give Asian Kitchen a try. We will definitely be back when we get to HCM City next time :-)

Their were also some shady locals looking to rob us. Obviously they didn't because they knew it would be too much work for them due to my size and the fact that I actually look like a fighter. Another very important point to make, in that long dark alley, there were many restaurants and one of them actually was named Asian Kitchen. However, it looked nothing like the pictures. I used my phone's GPS and saw that we were about 3 side streets parallel to the actual restaurant. They were trying to cash in on unsuspecting tourists.

7. To sum up point number 6. Asian Kitchen is located in the middle of an alley / side street. This alley / side street is located directly in front of the busy tourist hot spot. Safe area... Much safer then the alley we were originally in. Also the alley and the restaurant are filled with tourists and back packers. The restaurant itself is filled with tourists. That's how you know you are in the right spot.

8. Now on to the food. Being a CrossFit athlete and fighter, I can tell you that the food was clean. It looked and tasted fresh. 

9. On to the food.... The mango salad tasted better then any restaurant back home and any restaurant we've already been to in HCMC. The chicken stir fry and beef dish was perfect!

10. We got 3 dishes and one bottle water for under $11.50 Canadian. That was more then enough food for both of us. 

11. The staff all speak English and we're incredibly nice. All other restaurants we've been to, the staff was average at best and they all tried to over charge us... Every Vietnamese restaurant tried to over charge us. But, my local Vietnamese wife was not going to allow that!!! 

I give you my word, this place is perfect. We are already planning to come here every night for the remainder of our 10 days here. So many dishes to try. Will never get bored. Also, if you find a restaurant that you like after experiencing so many bad restaurants, why keep experimenting????

I can get everything in this perfect little restaurant that I could get anywhere else, the only difference....I get quality and quantity without spending an arm or leg. Or without spending the night in the bathroom.

Like I said earlier, I'm not a back packer or a budget traveler and therefore most places that people rave about will not appeal to me. I want quality and quantity and I get both and surprisingly cheap!!!!

No offence to the budget traveler or the back packer. Or mind set is very different. I am not looking for a deal especially when it is going into my mouth.

After a month doing volunteer work with a friend in Da Nang we had but one night in Ho Chi Minh City. The back-pack area is crammed with restaurants of all shapes and sizes and finding a good one that is to your taste is really kind of luck of the draw.

I think we won. Down a quiet alley we found a small place with a number of foreigners who seemed to be enjoying themselves, and with only that to guide us, we went in.
